evals.prompt: Design the search results page with filters for a vacation rental site I'm building.
evals.expected_output: Presents a Proven option drawn from patterns.md (chip row for top filters, panel with histogram price slider and a live-count apply button, text-link reset, empty state that names the cause with a one-tap fix), a Fit option, optionally a Stretch. Each labelled with a dial position and the products that informed it (Airbnb, Redfin, Booking.com). Says the profile is in training. Runs or names the function checks. No borrowed brand styling.
evals.baseline_note: Plain frontend-design avoids conventions and tends to invent a distinctive filter UI with no live count and no empty-state fix.

evals.prompt: I picked the sidebar filters over the panel for the admin tool, it's faster for power users. Log it.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/log_choice.py with context dashboard, job search + filters, attribute 'filter panel vs sidebar', picked sidebar, dial 1 or 2, source shown, why 'faster for power users'. No client names or data.
evals.baseline_note: Without the skill there is no decision log; the choice is lost.

evals.prompt: Make the sign-in screen for my habit tracker app. Keep it at dial 1.
evals.expected_output: One identifier-first door ('Log in or sign up' style), one field, Continue at 48 px or more, social sign-in as secondary below (canon 8, Airbnb and Uber). Touch targets 44 pt or more, AA contrast, checked by scripts/check.mjs. Near-black text is allowed (canon 12) even though frontend-design lists tinted near-black as a tell.
evals.baseline_note: Plain frontend-design would push for a distinctive look and may split sign-in and sign-up.
